A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCGS research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices—A–M in v1 and A–P in v2—support reliable comparison across additions, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices K–M report original ImageNet conversion accuracy, energy estimates, and coding and threshold-selection ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original COCO detection and PascalVOC segmentation evaluations and ablations in Appendices N–O.

M1.justification: Equation (6) and Appendix J add a zero-output condition between the smallest negative and positive thresholds; v1's stated rule always selects a nearest threshold. This changes the specified firing behavior. The differential-coding updates and threshold-iteration algorithm remain unchanged; the hardware variants are presented as equivalent implementations.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates ImageNet classification only. V2 retains this coverage and adds COCO object detection and PascalVOC semantic segmentation, substantially extending the evaluated task requirements beyond classification.

E2.justification: The ImageNet comparison retains TS, SNM, MMSE, QCFS, SRP, MST, STA, SpikeZIP-TF, and ECMT. The new task ablations reuse rate coding and 99.9% large-activation threshold selection; the added detector and segmenter architectures are conversion targets, not new competing conversion methods.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce COCO mAP at IoU 0.50–0.95 and PascalVOC mIoU, measured at T=2,4,6,8 with ResNet50-based architectures and threshold-count configurations including n=2,4,8. These are settings for new experiments; the existing ImageNet configurations and energy-estimation assumptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds FCOS and FCN ablations separately substituting rate coding or 99.9% large-activation thresholds (Tables 8 and 10), plus threshold-count sweeps in Tables 7 and 9. These extend the existing ablation questions to the new tasks. The ImageNet analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The activation-distribution variance used in the threshold theory is retained and does not constitute experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 7–10 add substantial detection and segmentation results; for example, FCOS ResNet50 with n=8 at T=6 reports 39.2% mAP and a 0.61 energy ratio. The ImageNet appendix values remain unchanged. The comparison table adds source ANN accuracies and changes SRP's VGG-16 accuracy at T=4 from 66.46% to 66.47%.

T1.justification: Appendix I substantively replaces the proof supporting the global-optimal-threshold guarantee. V1 argues that f is monotonically increasing; v2 revises its first derivative, introduces second-derivative and boundary analysis, and argues that f decreases before increasing toward zero. Appendices E–F also correct time and layer indices. The theorem statement and Gaussian activation assumption remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 adds an explicit introduction contribution claiming two equivalent, hardware-friendly MT-neuron implementations. The central claims about training-free differential coding, threshold iteration, accuracy, and energy efficiency remain substantively unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 argues that indexed sparse events and weight bit shifts preserve asynchronous, event-driven execution, and distinguishes weighted GPU outputs from a binary-channel realization. This adds substantive applicability discussion. The existing negative-threshold requirement and lack of optimal Transformer thresholds remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's conversion pseudocode and neuron equations, v2 supplies a source-code repository pointer, identifies the GPU output representation, and provides float32 bit-manipulation pseudocode in Appendix P. Section 4.3 documents normalization, threshold-index communication, and memory overhead; Appendices N–O identify torchvision as the source of the added models.

R1.justification: V2 adds background citations on direct SNN training and event-based vision, including Duan et al. (2022) and Shi et al. (2024), plus adaptive calibration by Wang et al. (2025) and the Speck hardware work by Yao et al. (2024). These extend background and hardware positioning without substantially redefining the relationship to existing conversion methods.

P1.justification: V2 adds Section 4.3, Appendices N–P, explicit proof steps, brief introduction additions, affiliations, correspondence information, and acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the overall progression through related work, method, experiments, and conclusion are retained.

P2.justification: V1's main ablation Tables 3–4 become dual-axis Figures 4–5, while detailed appendix tables remain. V2 expands the comparison table with an ANN-accuracy column, redraws Figure 1 with a synapse stage, adds four task-result tables and Algorithm 3, and substantially reformats the dense appendix derivations.

improvement.justification: Source ANN accuracies and controlled COCO/PascalVOC evaluations improve comparison transparency and applicability evidence beyond v1's ImageNet-only evaluation. The code pointer and GPU pseudocode also aid reproducibility. However, the new implementation descriptions contain a concrete inconsistency: with theta=1, n=4 and potential 0.1, Equation (6) gives zero while Algorithm 3 emits 0.125. This limits the implementation contribution's reliability, making the net quality improvement modest.
